thesis: AXT's Q2 2026 results (revenue $47.6M, +164% YoY; GAAP gross margin 44.9% vs 8.0% a year ago) and the July 29 Lumentum long-term InP supply agreement (with a disclosed $43.5M upfront deposit) confirm AI-datacenter optical demand is now showing up in disclosed financials, not just narrative; AXT is also set to join the S&P SmallCap 600 on Sept 21, 2026. The clearest counter-case is that Q3 guidance (~$66M) explicitly conditions further upside on China Ministry of Commerce export permits for InP/GaAs/Ge, and a Q4 2025 guidance miss was directly tied to permit delays -- but the already-signed long-term supply contracts and deposit money already in hand indicate the underlying demand this thesis rests on is intact even if permit timing slips a quarter.
invalidation: China export-permit approvals stall again and Q3 2026 guidance (due ~Oct 29) is walked back, or the Nowakowski securities suit is refiled with a scheduled hearing

thesis: Marvell's Aug 27 Q2 FY2027 results were a confirmed, company-disclosed beat-and-raise: record revenue $2.74B (+37% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.94 vs $0.87 est., Q3 guide $3.15B/$1.10 EPS, and raised FY2027/FY2028 outlooks on AI custom-silicon demand. However, the same Aug 19 disclosure that unlocked the Google chip-supply deal also granted Google a warrant for up to ~58.97M MRVL shares (~6.4% potential dilution) contingent on future purchase milestones -- a disclosed dilution risk that keeps this at low conviction under our fixed rubric regardless of the earnings strength. Customer concentration (~82% of revenue from top-10 customers, chiefly hyperscalers) is the standing bear case Erste Group cited in its July 14 downgrade to Hold.
invalidation: Google warrant dilution materializes without commensurate revenue growth, or a top hyperscaler customer pulls back orders

thesis: NVIDIA's Aug 26 Q2 FY2027 results (revenue $96.2B, +106% YoY; Data Center $89.0B, +117% YoY) and the Sept 2 definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93B are the clearest disclosed positives, but the picture is mixed rather than dominant: China continues restricting H200 purchases (already excluded from guidance), a France antitrust probe is reportedly 'nearing the end' with no scheduled ruling date, and a fund manager's 'crowded AI trade' warning coincided with a brief pullback this week. No single factor -- the acquisition, the China friction, or the sentiment chatter -- is resolved as clearly dominant, so this sits at medium rather than high.
invalidation: Q3 FY2027 guidance (due ~Nov 25) disappoints, or China export restrictions widen beyond what's already priced into guidance

thesis: SK hynix's rally traces to a confirmed, disclosed catalyst: the Nvidia HBM4 supply lock-in (~70% of Nvidia's HBM4 orders through 2030, part of a reported $500B AI memory deal) plus Q2 2026 results confirming an HBM-led 'memory supercycle.' But SK hynix completed a $26.5B Nasdaq ADR offering in July 2026 (~2.5% dilution via third-party allotment) inside our 90-day disclosure window, which is a disclosed dilution risk that caps this at low conviction under our fixed rubric regardless of the demand story's strength. A DRAM price-fixing class action (filed June 25) and a criminal breach-of-trust probe into the CEO (opened Aug 5) are both open-ended with no scheduled hearing date, so neither is flagged as active_litigation.
invalidation: HBM/DRAM pricing rolls over as 2027-28 capacity additions come online, or Q3 2026 earnings (~Oct 27) walk back supercycle guidance

thesis: BWIN's price/volume spike is fully explained by a confirmed, disclosed catalyst -- a Sept 14 definitive agreement to go private via Sequence Holdings and Michael Dell's family office (DFO Management) at $32.50/share cash, ~$7.7B deal value. Current price (~$32.06) is trading essentially at the deal price, so the 'near 52-week-high' and volume signals are a merger-arbitrage ceiling and closing-related volume, not organic bullish momentum -- a mechanical explanation that caps this at low conviction and argues against treating it as a fresh long entry. Multiple plaintiff firms have opened fairness investigations into the buyout price, but none has a scheduled hearing or ruling yet.
invalidation: deal is renegotiated, terminated, or a topping bid emerges before the expected Q1 2027 close

thesis: Dell's rally is anchored to a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: the Q2 FY2027 earnings release (Sept 1) disclosing a $95B server order backlog including ~$16.4B of AI-dedicated servers sold last quarter, reinforced by RBC's Sept 11 Outperform initiation ($640 PT) citing that same backlog. Today's fresh all-time high extends the same disclosed thesis rather than reflecting a new event. The clearest counter-case is margin compression -- gross margin fell to 17.8% from 21.1% YoY as low-margin AI servers dilute the mix, and DELL fell ~6.85% on Sept 14 amid AI-slowdown chatter from other tech executives -- but that Sept 14 move was driven by sector-wide sentiment, not a Dell-specific disclosure, and doesn't offset the multi-year revenue visibility the backlog itself represents.
invalidation: Q3 FY2027 earnings (~Nov 24) show backlog growth stalling or gross margin deteriorating further

thesis: FANG's volume spike and today's ~7.65% drop reflect a mix of a Morgan Stanley downgrade to Equalweight (analyst opinion, not a company disclosure), a disclosed insider sale by Executive Chairman Travis Stice (~75,000 shares), and a broad energy-sector selloff after OPEC/IEA cut 2026 oil demand forecasts and US crude inventories built -- the same day multiple Permian peers (Permian Resources, APA, Viper Energy) also fell. This is explicitly a macro/sector-wide move layered on a single downgrade, not a company-specific fundamental deterioration -- Q2 2026 results actually beat ($6.48 EPS) and UBS raised its target to $253 just two days before the drop -- so the picture is mixed/offsetting rather than a clear directional read.
invalidation: oil prices stabilize/rebound and the stock recovers with peers, or a genuine company-specific negative disclosure emerges

thesis: KNX's drop and volume spike track a sector-wide reaction to J.B. Hunt's conference warning about Q3 earnings pressure from diesel/driver-cost inflation (JBHT fell ~10-13%, dragging peers including KNX, ODFL, XPO, SNDR), compounded by a same-day Fed rate hike that sent the broader market down (Dow -631 pts). This is explicitly a macro/sector-wide catalyst, not a KNX-specific disclosure -- no KNX-specific news (earnings, guidance change, executive move) was found today, and FreightWaves reporting describes improving truckload fundamentals (rate/mile gains, tightening capacity) into Q3 -- so the read is mixed rather than a clear bearish signal on the company itself.
invalidation: diesel prices/driver costs continue outpacing rate repricing into KNX's own Q3 2026 results (expected late Oct 2026)

thesis: SPCX's 60-day gain follows SpaceX's actual June 12, 2026 Nasdaq IPO (not a synthetic tracker), with near-term flows dominated by mechanical drivers rather than a fresh fundamental disclosure: a Nasdaq-100 rebalance effective Sept 21 is expected to force passive buying as SPCX's index weight roughly doubles, and an unresolved binary event -- SpaceX's first Starship orbital attempt, scheduled Sept 22 -- could move the stock sharply either way before its outcome is known. Musk himself was reported to have warned employees of a 'genuine risk of bankruptcy' if Raptor engine production doesn't scale fast enough, which is going-concern-adjacent language from the CEO. Staggered post-IPO lockup unlocks (the Sept 9 unlock already drove a ~3.9% drop; the next is Sept 24) add ongoing share-supply overhang.
invalidation: would revisit if Starship Flight 14 succeeds and lockup unlock supply is absorbed without price pressure
